g.text: Binary rewards, group of 8. GRPO divides the group-centred reward by the group standard deviation, and for a Bernoulli group

text.style: font-size: 9.5px; font-family: 'Segoe UI', 'DejaVu Sans'; fill: #475569

g.text: that standard deviation is smallest exactly where the prompt is nearly always solved or nearly never solved -- the prompts

text.style: font-size: 9.5px; font-family: 'Segoe UI', 'DejaVu Sans'; fill: #475569

g.text: with the least left to teach. The division therefore scales their gradients up by 1/sigma while a prompt at the 50% frontier,

text.style: font-size: 9.5px; font-family: 'Segoe UI', 'DejaVu Sans'; fill: #475569

g.text: the informative one, gets the smallest weight. Dr. GRPO's fix is to drop the division and centre only. A group that is all

text.style: font-size: 9.5px; font-family: 'Segoe UI', 'DejaVu Sans'; fill: #475569

g.text: right or all wrong has zero variance and contributes nothing either way.
